note: Each entry names a defect class the departments' skills (data/knowledge/code-safety/) look for, a regex that finds a candidate insertion site, and a string template that introduces the defect at that site. seed-defects.mjs is the generic interpreter: it applies sitePattern per line, filters by fileRequirePattern/fileExcludePattern/fieldHintPattern, and fills insertTemplate's {{placeholders}}. {{indent}} is the site line's leading whitespace, {{source}} and {{field}} are sitePattern's first and second capture groups (the matched req.<source>.<field> in the javascript entries; the declared constant and the object it was read from in the typescript entries; absent for the hardcoded-credential entries), {{line}} is the 1-based line number of the site (for unique identifier names), and {{hex}} is a seeded pseudo-random 32-character hex string (hardcoded-credential only).

entries.description: Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field>; inserted code passes that same field to eval(), mirroring NodeGoat's own app/routes/contributions.js#eval(req.body.preTax) pattern generalized to any field, as if the field could carry a simple arithmetic expression.

Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field>; inserted code builds a MongoDB $where clause by concatenating that field into a JavaScript-evaluated string, mirroring NodeGoat's own app/data/allocations-dao.js threshold filter.
Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field>; inserted code hands that same field to fetch() as the request URL with no host allowlist, a fire-and-forget webhook-ping shape.

Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field>; inserted code writes that field into a console.log line with no control-character stripping, mirroring NodeGoat's own app/routes/session.js login-username log line.

Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field> in a file that also calls res.<something> elsewhere (so a res parameter is in scope); inserted code redirects to that field with no destination check, mirroring NodeGoat's own app/routes/index.js /learn redirect.
Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field>; inserted code compiles that field directly into a RegExp, the new RegExp(userInput) pattern the injection skill names explicitly.

Sites are lines that reference req.query/body/params.<field> in a file that also calls res.<something> elsewhere (so a res parameter is in scope); inserted code concatenates that field straight into an HTML response with no escaping.

Sites are a file's own `const X = require('y');` lines, however the required value is then used (no request field needed); inserted code declares a secret with a hardcoded fallback used when the environment variable is unset, the process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'literal' pattern the secrets skill names explicitly.

Sites are lines that declare a constant from a value read off an external process's wire message (params, message, record, response, update, notification, item, turn, thread, terminal, session); inserted code writes that constant into a stderr log line with no control-character stripping, the TypeScript counterpart of the javascript log-injection entry.

Sites are lines that declare a constant from a value read off an external process's wire message; inserted code passes that constant to eval(), the TypeScript counterpart of the javascript eval-injection entry.

Sites are lines that declare a constant from a value read off an external process's wire message; inserted code compiles that constant directly into a RegExp, the new RegExp(userInput) pattern the injection skill names explicitly.

Sites are a module's own single-line exported constants (no request field needed); inserted code declares a secret with a hardcoded fallback used when the environment variable is unset, the process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'literal' pattern the secrets skill names explicitly.
